Hi Andreia, it's Paul from Boston. Before Thursday's meeting, I want to explain my position, so there are no surprises. I think we should cut the simulator training for new nurses from forty hours to twenty. Although the simulator is a great tool, forty hours is a lot of time for nurses who are already very busy. Our budget is also smaller this year, and we need to save money somewhere. Despite that, I know this training is important to you and to your team. So I am open to a real debate. Please bring your data and your best arguments. If your argument is compelling, I am happy to change my mind. See you on Thursday.

Thank you, Paul. I understand your concern, and your point about the budget is valid. But I stand by my position: new nurses need forty hours on the simulator. Although the training takes time, it reduces errors in the operating room. Last year, the nurses with forty hours of practice were faster and more confident in real surgeries. Even though twenty hours looks cheaper, one mistake with a patient costs much more. So, despite the smaller budget, I believe the benefits outweigh the costs. Here is my proposal: forty hours for new nurses and twenty hours for experienced nurses. I think that is common ground for all of us.

Here is how Andreia defends her position in the meeting. First, she makes a clear claim: new nurses need forty hours of training. Then she accepts that Paul's point about the budget is valid. Next, she gives her counterargument with real data from last year. After that, she explains why the benefits outweigh the costs. Finally, she proposes some common ground for both teams.
